claim: AI buildout demand for power and materials could make energy and commodities such as copper a simple, liquid and leverageable way to get AI exposure that investors are overlooking.
drivers: copper demand for electrification and grid build-out
kill_criteria: AI-related demand turns out to be a small share of power or copper demand growth

research.question: How large is AI/data-center demand relative to total power and copper demand growth over the next five years?
research.why: The thesis only works if AI is a material driver of these markets.

research.question: Which liquid instruments give leveraged AI exposure through power and copper (copper futures and ETFs such as COPX/CPER, uranium such as URA/CCJ, utilities via XLU, independent power producers VST/CEG/TLN, grid equipment such as GEV/ETN/PWR), and how much of each one's revenue or price driver is actually AI?
research.why: The thesis claims a simple, liquid, leverageable expression exists; we need specific instruments and their AI sensitivity.

research.question: Since 2023, how correlated have those energy and commodity instruments been with AI equities (e.g. NVDA, SMH), and did they behave like AI proxies in AI drawdowns such as the January 2025 DeepSeek selloff?
research.why: If they already trade as AI beta, the overlooked claim fails; if they don't, they are not AI exposure.

research.question: What supply constraints (copper mine supply and grades, gas turbine and transformer backlogs, interconnection queues, nuclear restarts) determine whether AI demand turns into price and margin for these instruments?
research.why: Demand only becomes returns where supply is constrained.

research.question: What evidence would prove the thesis wrong: AI efficiency gains reducing power demand, data-center capex cuts, consensus forecasts already pricing the demand, or non-AI drivers (China property, EVs) dominating copper?
research.why: Kill criteria need concrete observable tests.

research.question: For copper futures (COMEX HG), CPER, COPX, URA and the IPPs, what are the fees, roll costs, margin or embedded leverage, liquidity and tax treatment, and which gives the 'fee-free, liquid, leverageable' exposure Manidis describes?
research.why: The thesis's 'simple, liquid, leverageable' claim needs instrument-level terms before any recommendation.

research.question: Track quarterly: hyperscaler capex guidance, US utility large-load interconnection requests, and IPP data-center contract announcements; does any print show AI power demand plateauing?
research.why: Recurring monitor for the power-leg kill criterion.

research.question: What share of total copper demand growth to 2030 (not total demand) comes from data centres, using one source's base-year and 2030 totals?
research.why: The kill criterion is about share of demand growth; the IEA 2% figure is share of total demand (Codex P1 on omnibrain #8).

research.question: For VST, CEG, TLN, GEV, ETN, PWR, CCJ/URA and XLU: what share of revenue, contracted volume or backlog is attributable to AI/data centres?
research.why: Cycle 1 answered this only for CEG/TLN contracts and GEV's 20% gas share; the rest of the instrument-exposure scope is open (Codex P2 on omnibrain #8).

risks: AI capex slows or is already priced into energy and copper
commodity prices are driven mostly by factors unrelated to AI

evidence.quote: Constellation Energy, Talen Energy and GE Vernova tumbled more than 20%

updates.summary: Power equities already behave like AI stocks: on 2025-01-27 VST fell ~28-30% and CEG/TLN/GEV >20% (CNBC), worse than NVDA (-17%) and SMH (-10%). Agent computation on Yahoo Finance daily closes 2023-01-04..2026-10-20 (not a quoted source): daily-return correlation with SMH is GEV 0.61, COPX 0.53, URA 0.52, VST 0.49, CEG 0.48, CPER 0.36, copper futures 0.28, XLU 0.10; beta to SMH GEV 0.99, VST 0.72, CEG 0.64, copper futures 0.22. Copper futures fell only ~2% on the DeepSeek day. So the power names are crowded AI beta (not overlooked) and copper is mostly not AI beta. [research worker w-6fbe728b80a0]

evidence.quote: wait times for critical grid components such as transformers and cables have doubled in the past three years
Turbine deliveries for new gas-fired power plants now face lead times of several years

claim.text: Wait times for transformers and cables have doubled and turbine deliveries face multi-year lead times.
GE Vernova has gas equipment agreements signed into 2031.

evidence.quote: widening from about 104 000 metric tons in 2026 to 368 000 metric tons in 2027

claim.text: ICSG forecasts refined copper surpluses in 2026 and 2027.

updates.summary: Power-side supply is tight: IEA says transformer and cable wait times doubled in three years and gas-turbine deliveries face multi-year lead times; GE Vernova has gas agreements signed into 2031. Copper is tight only on BNEF's long horizon (6 Mt shortfall by 2035); ICSG (Oct 2026) sees refined surpluses of ~104 kt in 2026 and ~368 kt in 2027. The constraint, and so the pricing power, sits in power equipment and generation, not near-term copper. [research worker w-5816eee86ccb]

evidence.quote: electricity demand from data centres is 20% lower in 2035 than in the Base Case

claim.text: In the IEA High Efficiency Case data-centre electricity demand is 20% lower in 2035.

updates.summary: Observable kill tests: (1) copper leg is already near its kill criterion, AI is ~2% of 2030 copper demand (IEA) and ICSG sees surpluses through 2027; (2) power leg: an efficiency shock like DeepSeek (VST -~30% in a day) or the IEA High Efficiency Case (-20% data-centre demand by 2035) would break it; (3) 'overlooked' fails if power names keep trading as AI beta (beta to SMH 0.6-1.0, agent computation). Proposed sharper kill criteria are in the review packet for Noah. [research worker w-014dbb2df372]

Correction to the 2026-10-21 research updates after review: (1) the kill criterion is not established for copper, because the IEA ~512 kt / ~2% figure is a share of total copper demand, not of demand growth (task 416ae73b4d50 computes the growth share); (2) the US 'nearly half of demand growth' figure is all data-centre load, not AI-only load, so the power side is unresolved too; (3) GEV beta to SMH is 0.84 when covariance and variance use the same dates, not 0.99. The view's kill criterion is unknown.
